thread:
Maria Chen: heads up — after the key-canonicalization roll at 03:15 we saw a sustained TTL oscillation on prefix cache entries and a backend RPS surge. p95 tokens latency jumped ~2.8x for a few minutes.
Jon Patel: saw that. kv-monitor shows a 4x increase in miss rate and backend connections spiked. any obvious diff in key cardinality?
Deepak Rao: digging into histogram — cardinality for english prefixes up ~3.2x, non-english up ~6x. canonicalization dropped some aggressive collapsing we relied on.
Rachel Kim: quick question — did the deploy change namespace hashing or remove a normalization step? that would fragment hot prefixes.
Maria Chen: it removed unicode NFKC normalization to speed up tokenization path. idea was to avoid the normalization CPU cost, but it created multiple variants for same logical prefix.
Alyssa (infra): kv-monitor-bot logs:
```
KV misses: baseline 6% -> 27%
Backend RPS: 4200 -> 22k
Active conns: 62 -> 310
prefetch queue depth: 0 -> 480
```
Jon Patel: prefetcher was disabled in the same deploy? I remember a flag flip for async warmup.
Maria Chen: yes — to reduce contention we turned off async prefetch in the same PR. combination = canonicalization fragmentation + no prefetch -> synchronous miss flood.
Deepak Rao: profiling snapshot attached: kernel selection time unaffected, but observed batcher backpressure. many small requests bypassing batching heuristics because miss latency is dominated by redis/TCP, not GPU.
Rachel Kim: suggestion: roll back the normalization removal first, re-enable async prefetcher as a short-term mitigation, and throttle backend by adding a light-weight local bloom filter to absorb obvious duplicates.
Alyssa (infra): deploy-bot: rollback started for commit ab12f3 — will revert canonicalization change. ETA ~8m. :hourglass:
Maria Chen: while rollback in progress, can we emergency-adjust batching heuristics to prefer slightly larger batch windows for prefixes with low KV hit-rate? that should reduce backend QPS.
Jon Patel: can do. patch to batcher to increase max wait from 6ms -> 12ms for requests with cache_miss_hint=true. pushing now to canary.
Deepak Rao: also adding a short TTL jitterization to avoid synchronized eviction at the cache side. propose adding random(0, TTL/10) to entry TTLs.
Rachel Kim: agree on jitter. also add quick telemetry: emit cache_key_variant_count per prefix hash so we know fragmentation level next time.
Maria Chen: current mitigation checklist:
- rollback canonicalization (in flight)
- re-enable async prefetcher (manual flip after rollback) — Alyssa to coordinate
- bump batcher max wait for miss-prone prefixes (Jon pushing)
- add TTL jitter and variant_count metric (Deepak/Rachel)
- soft-rate-limit incoming unrouted requests to 60% until backend stabilizes
Alyssa (infra): rollback completed at 03:23, kv-monitor-bot shows miss rate trending down.
kv-monitor-bot: KV misses: 27% -> 9% over 180s. Backend RPS: 22k -> 6.1k. connections -> 78.
Maria Chen: good. follow-up actions: open perf PR to reintroduce canonicalization in safe form (NFKC only for ascii+common scripts, maintain a canonical map), add unit tests for key collapse, and make prefetch default-on with a circuit-breaker rather than full-off.
Jon Patel: noted — I'll land the batching tweak and a canary dashboard for batch size vs miss-rate.
Deepak Rao: I'll file an eval to simulate fragmentations and run kernel fallback scenarios. want to validate we don't cause additional batching regressions when we change batch timing.
Rachel Kim: add ops runbook steps: (1) check variant_count metric, (2) flip prefetch flag, (3) throttle ingress if backend>2k RPS, (4) rollback canonicalization commit id.
Maria Chen: postmortem owners: Deepak (root cause/profiling), Jon (batching fixes), Rachel (metrics & runbook), Alyssa (deploy coordination). will draft follow-up doc with timelines and graphs.
Jon Patel: quick note — observed one oddity: some long-tail users still had higher p99 after rollback; likely due to warmed kv clients being evicted earlier. recommend a targeted prefetch for top-500 hot prefixes for 10m after deploy.
Maria Chen: agreed. let's schedule the prefetch sweep after the rollback stabilizes. thanks all.
kv-monitor-bot: alert cleared. incident duration ~12m.
deploy-bot: rollback ab12f3 -> success at 03:23:14"
